rubric.why: Identifies the symbols used for enthalpy and enthalpy change.
rubric.description: Enthalpy is represented by H, while enthalpy change is represented by ΔH.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for correctly distinguishing H from ΔH.

rubric.why: States the difference in whether the two quantities can be measured directly.
rubric.description: The total enthalpy cannot be measured directly, but the change in enthalpy can be measured comparatively easily.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating both measurement facts.

modelAnswer: Enthalpy of a system is represented by (H) while the change in enthalpy which a system undergoes is represented by ΔH. The total enthalpy (H) of a system cannot be measured directly. However, the change in enthalpy ΔH brought about in a system can be measured comparatively easily.

rubric.why: Identifies that breaking bonds requires energy.
rubric.description: Breaking bonds of H₂ and O₂ absorbs energy.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that bond breaking absorbs or requires energy.

rubric.why: Connects energy absorption during bond breaking with the endothermic process.
rubric.description: Energy absorption makes bond breaking an endothermic process.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying bond breaking as endothermic because energy is absorbed.

modelAnswer: Breaking of bonds of H₂ and O₂ absorb energy (endothermic process) while making of bonds between H and O evolve energy (exothermic process).

rubric.why: Includes the reactants and product in the reaction representation.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for correctly representing the reaction and its product.

rubric.why: Represents the transition state and indicates bonds breaking and forming.
rubric.description: Shows the transition state in brackets, with dotted bonds indicating bonds breaking and forming.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a bracketed transition state with dotted or otherwise clearly indicated partial bonds.

modelAnswer: H—H + Cl—Cl ⟶ [H···H···Cl···Cl]‡ ⟶ 2H—Cl. Show the transition state in brackets, with bonds breaking and forming represented by dotted lines.

rubric.why: Identifies glycogen's role as a glucose-storage material.
rubric.description: Glycogen is the primary storage form of glucose.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that glycogen stores glucose.

rubric.why: Names the body's main locations where glycogen is stored.
rubric.description: Glycogen is stored in the liver and muscles.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming both the liver and muscles.

modelAnswer: Glycogen is the primary storage form of glucose. It is stored in the liver and muscles.

rubric.why: Identifies why the reaction does not take place under ordinary conditions.
rubric.description: The reaction between atmospheric nitrogen and oxygen is highly endothermic.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the reaction is highly endothermic.

rubric.why: Explains how lightning enables the reaction to occur.
rubric.description: Lightning provides enough energy for the reaction to take place and produce nitric oxide.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that lightning supplies the energy needed for the reaction.

modelAnswer: Nitrogen of the atmosphere reacts with oxygen to produce nitric oxide in the presence of lightning. This is because reaction is highly endothermic, so only lightning can provide enough energy for this reaction to take place.

rubric.why: Defines heat as energy transferred because of a temperature difference.
rubric.description: Heat is energy that flows from a hot body to a cold body because of a difference in temperature.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing heat as thermal energy transferred due to a temperature difference.

rubric.why: Distinguishes enthalpy as a property of a system, or states its relationship to heat at constant pressure.
rubric.description: Enthalpy is an essential part of a system and depends on its molecules, composition and structure; at constant pressure, enthalpy change equals heat evolved or absorbed.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying enthalpy as a system property or stating that at constant pressure enthalpy change equals heat evolved or absorbed.

modelAnswer: Heat is a form of energy that flows from hot body to a cold body because of a difference in temperature. We measure heat in joules. Heat is what we call the transfer of thermal energy. Contrary to this, enthalpy is an essential part of a system since it depends on the number of molecules present in that system, its chemical composition and its structure. Heat is not essential part of a system, it just comes and goes. When heat leaves or enters a system, it results in a change of enthalpy. At a constant pressure the enthalpy change is equal to heat evolved or absorbed.

rubric.why: States what happens to energy when a bond forms.
rubric.description: Energy is evolved when a bond is formed.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that bond formation releases or evolves energy.

rubric.why: Connects energy release during bond formation to an exothermic process.
rubric.description: Bond formation is exothermic because heat is evolved.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying bond formation as exothermic due to heat evolution.

modelAnswer: Since energy is needed to break a bond while energy is evolved when a bond is formed, such reactions take place always with the evolution of heat.

rubric.why: Defines activation energy in relation to reaching the transition state.
rubric.description: Activation energy is the energy absorbed by reactant or product molecules to be converted into the transition state.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for defining activation energy as the energy required or absorbed to reach the transition state.

rubric.why: Identifies the transition state on the energy curve and defines aerobic respiration.
rubric.description: The transition state is at the peak of the curve; respiration in the presence of oxygen is aerobic respiration.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for locating the transition state at the curve's peak and/or defining aerobic respiration as respiration in oxygen.

modelAnswer: The energy absorbed by the reactant or product molecules in order to be converted into the transition state is called the activation energy (Eₐ) of the reaction. The transition state is shown at the peak of curve in Fig. (5.4). This process that occurs in the presence of oxygen is called aerobic respiration.
